newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH KYRO PLANS SHARE ISSUE, BOURSE LISTING. [CORRECTED 13:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: FINNISH KYRO PLANS SHARE ISSUE, BOURSE LISTING. [CORRECTED 13:00 GMT]

text.p: Finnish machinery and power firm (corrects industry from forestry) Kyro Oy said in a statement on Monday its board would propose to the annual general meeting an issue of up to 8.18 million new shares and a subsequent application for a bourse listing.
"The board of Kyro has decided ... to apply for a listing of the company's shares on the bourse list of the Helsinki Stock Exchange," Kyro said.

"The board is proposing to the April 15, 1997 annual general meeting that the share capital be raised by offering shares to institutional investors and the public for subscription between May 19 and May 28, 1997," it said.

At least 5.00 million and at most 8.175 million new shares, each with a nominal value of 1.00 markka, would be offered for subscription. An extraordinary shareholders' meeting on May 30 will set the subscription price based on a book-building period.
Kyro said its comparable net sales increased 34.6 percent in 1996 over 1995 to 818.6 million markka with exports and overseas operations accounting for 79.5 percent.

Operating profit was 103.6 million markka and profit after financial items was 100.8 million. Return on investment rose to 18.4 percent from 16.2 percent in 1995, and ROE rose to 16.9 percent from 13.6 percent.
"The market prospects are favourable for the group's areas of operation," Kyro said.
